title: The American Civil War
competency: Outline slavery as the main divisive issue, the major steps of the American Civil War and its consequences.

ideas.name: Origins of the American Civil War

en.text: The Civil War (1861–1865) pitted mostly 23 northern Union states against 11 southern states that seceded as the Confederate States of America. The issues were Southern resentment of Northern economic dominance, tariffs, states' rights against federal power and, above all, slavery, the only issue able to cause secession. The Republican Party (1854) opposed slavery in the western territories; when its candidate Abraham Lincoln was elected in 1860, seven states seceded and formed the Confederacy in February 1861. Lincoln took office on 4 March 1861.

screens.title: Which tax suits whom?
screens.ask: The North had growing industries; the South grew cotton and bought European goods. Which tariff policy would each want?
opts: North: protective tariffs; South: low tariffs
screens.after: Tariffs protected Northern industry but made the South's imports dearer.

screens.title: North against South
paras: The war lasted from 1861 to 1865.
On one side: mostly the 23 northern states of the Union.
On the other: the Confederate States of America.
It was made up of 11 southern states that declared secession.

screens.title: Divisive issues
paras: Slavery outweighed all other issues.
It was the only issue able to cause secession and civil war.
table: low tariffs for cheap European imports

screens.title: The road to secession
paras: 1854: the Republican Party was founded.
It opposed slavery in the western territories.
Northerners and Westerners did not want to compete with slave labour.
1860: Abraham Lincoln, the Republican candidate, was elected President.
He was self-educated, an able speaker and an effective politician.
The South saw his election as an intolerable threat to slavery.
Seven states seceded and formed the Confederate States of America (February 1861).
They seized federal forts and property.
4 March 1861: Lincoln was sworn in and called secession "legally void".
screens.note: The book dates the Confederacy 9 February 1861; it was formally set up on 8 February, and Jefferson Davis was chosen president on 9 February.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.did: Republican; President of the USA from 4 March 1861. Issued the Emancipation Proclamation. Assassinated on 14 April 1865.

screens.title: North or South?
items: Resented the other side's economic dominance

screens.title: Put the road to war in order
screens.clue: Secession came before Lincoln took office.

screens.text: Why did Lincoln's election in 1860 trigger secession?
opts: The South had lost political control and feared attacks on slavery
Lincoln promised to invade the South at once
He had raised tariffs on cotton
screens.ans: The South had lost political control and feared attacks on slavery
screens.clue: What did the South fear for?

screens.text: Lincoln said he would not invade the South but would hold federal property. Why did war still follow?
opts: The Confederacy had seized federal forts, so holding them meant using force
Lincoln freed all slaves at once in 1861
screens.ans: The Confederacy had seized federal forts, so holding them meant using force
screens.why: p.18: the seceded states took federal forts; Lincoln called for troops to recapture them and preserve the Union.
screens.clue: Step 1: what had the seceded states taken? Step 2: what did Lincoln promise to keep?

en.text: The North had most advantages: more states and people, skilled labour, industry, railways, food, money and naval power to blockade the South; Britain and France did not intervene. The South had better generals at first and fought hard on defence. In September 1862 Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, freeing slaves in rebel territory from 1 January 1863, which brought African American troops to the North and kept Europe out. The Confederacy was defeated in April 1865; John Wilkes Booth killed Lincoln on 14 April 1865. About 620,000 died. The 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments abolished slavery and gave former slaves citizenship and the vote.

am.text: ሰሜኑ ብዙ ጥቅሞች ነበሩት። በ1862 የነፃነት አዋጅ ወጣ። በሚያዝያ 1865 ደቡቡ ተሸነፈ፤ ሊንከን ተገደለ። 13ኛው ማሻሻያ ባርነትን አስቀረ።

screens.title: Why so long?
screens.ask: The North had more people, factories, railways and money. Why did the war still last four years?
opts: The South had better generals at first and fought hard on defence
screens.after: Defensive firearms and determined Southern generals made the North's victory slow.

screens.title: Why the Union won
paras: The North had most of the advantages:
more states and a much bigger population;
more skilled labour, far more industry and railways;
more farm output (except cotton) and far more money;
naval power to blockade the South.
Britain and France sympathised with "king cotton" but did not intervene.
The South had better generals at first and great determination.
Firearms favoured defence, which helped the South.
The war (1861–1865) killed about 620,000 people.

screens.title: The Emancipation Proclamation
paras: At first the North fought to end secession, not slavery.
But slavery had caused secession, so both were causes.
September 1862: Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation.
From 1 January 1863, slaves in rebel-held territory were free.
The North recruited African American troops, who served with distinction.
Slaves were encouraged to flee the plantations.
No European government could now support the slave-holding South.

screens.title: The end and the results
paras: April 1865: the Confederacy was defeated completely.
14 April 1865: John Wilkes Booth, a southern fanatic, shot Lincoln.
The war ended secession and slavery for good.
Three amendments to the US Constitution followed:

screens.title: Whose advantage?

screens.text: How did the Emancipation Proclamation help the North?
opts: It brought in African American troops and kept Europe from aiding the South
It ended the war at once
It freed slaves in the North only
screens.ans: It brought in African American troops and kept Europe from aiding the South
screens.clue: Think of soldiers and of Europe.

screens.text: From the very start, the North fought mainly to end slavery.
screens.why: p.19: the North first fought to end secession; emancipation came in 1862–63.
screens.clue: What was the first war aim?

screens.text: Britain and France sympathised with the South's cotton economy. Why did making the war about slavery stop them helping it?
opts: Europe now saw slavery as wrong and indefensible, so backing the South became impossible
screens.ans: Europe now saw slavery as wrong and indefensible, so backing the South became impossible
screens.why: p.19: slavery was regarded in Europe as obsolete and totally wrong, so support for the Confederacy was politically and morally impossible.
screens.clue: Step 1: what did Europe think of slavery? Step 2: what would supporting the South then mean?

notes.text: p.18: the Confederacy is dated 9 February 1861; it was formally established on 8 February 1861 at Montgomery, and Jefferson Davis was chosen provisional president on 9 February. The lesson says "February 1861" with a note.
